name: Tear down a competitor's live Meta ads on demand with Bright Data, GPT-5.6 and an n8n form

parameters.content:
## Tear down a competitor's live ads, and find what you have no answer to

Anyone can look up a competitor in the Meta Ad Library. Nobody checks *how long* each ad has run - and nobody pays to keep a losing ad alive, so age is the scoreboard. On a live check a Club Pilates creative had been running 888 days while most of the grid was under 30.

### How it works

Fill in the form: their brand or your whole category, optionally your own brand, and a country. Both sides go through the same loop on the same day, so the comparison is like-for-like rather than two lookups you eyeball side by side.

Bright Data's Web Unlocker fetches each Ad Library search - no dataset, no snapshot, no polling. Every card is parsed out: library ID, advertiser, full primary text, button offer, creative, and the date it started running. The destination arrives wrapped in a Facebook redirect, so unwrapping it exposes the real landing page, the advertiser's own `utm_campaign` naming and any discount code.

Anything past your threshold is marked proven. Their proven offers with no equivalent in yours are flagged as gaps, the top landing pages are read to check the promise still matches the page, and two model calls name the angles and then the gap. The report renders in your browser when the run finishes; tick the email box and it is also sent.

### Setup

1. Bright Data: a Web Unlocker zone as Header Auth (`Authorization` / `Bearer <key>`). Free tier is 5,000 requests a month, no card.

2. An OpenAI credential. A Gmail credential only if you want the email.

3. Open the form's **Production URL** and fill it in. Nothing to schedule.

No spreadsheet, no stored state - each run stands alone.

## 1. Ask about one competitor
A form, not a schedule. You look this up when a pitch or a launch makes you want to know, and the answer comes back in the same browser tab.

## 2. One advertiser at a time
The loop's second output carries a search to Bright Data and the parser sends it back. Output zero fires once both sides are done.

## 3. Age is the scoreboard
Days running per ad, longest first, deduped. Nobody pays to run a losing ad for a year, so age is the only public proof an ad works.

## 4. Theirs against yours
Both sides came through the same loop on the same day, so the comparison is like-for-like. Their proven offers with no match in yours are flagged here.

## 5. What the page says now
The ad promises one thing; the landing page may have moved on. One read per domain, longest-running ad first.

## 6. Name the angle, then the gap
One model call names the offers that lasted. A second says which of them you have no answer to, and refuses to invent a gap when there is none.

## 7. Read it, and optionally keep it
The report renders in the browser of whoever asked. Tick the email box on the form and it is also sent, without changing what you see.

## One page of results, on purpose

The Ad Library loads more cards on scroll, which a single fetch cannot trigger, so each search returns the first 28-30 ads rather than all of them. That is the newest and most prominent slice, not a random sample - but a term with ~12,000 results is a category, not a competitor. Narrow it if you want coverage rather than a pulse.

Creatives lazy-load too, and how many arrive varies by fetch: across live runs between 1 and 23 cards in a page of 57 came through with no still image. Those are marked rather than dropped - the copy, the offer, the landing page and the days running are all still there, which is the part you act on.

Leave your own brand empty and you get a teardown with no comparison. The gap section says so rather than inventing one.

parameters.formDescription: Reads every ad they are running on Facebook and Instagram right now, ranks them by how long each has survived, and tells you which of their proven offers you have no answer to.

parameters.responseText:
={{ '

Nothing is running right now

No active ads came back for ' + $('Brief Me On A Competitor').first().json['Competitor brand or category'] + ' in ' + $('Brief Me On A Competitor').first().json['Country'] + '.

That is a finding rather than an error. Either they have paused everything, or they advertise under a different page name than the one you searched. Try the category they sell into instead of the brand.

parameters.text:
=You are reading competitor ads pulled live from the Meta Ad Library. Each one carries how many days it has been running, which is the only public evidence of whether it works - an ad that has run for months survived months of spend, and a two-week-old ad is an experiment.

Their ads:
{{ JSON.stringify($('Split Theirs From Yours').all().map(i => i.json).filter(r => r.side !== 'us').map(i => ({ advertiser: i.advertiser, days: i.days_running, text: String(i.ad_text || '').slice(0, 300), offer: i.offer, lands_on: i.landing_domain })).slice(0, 25)) }}

In under 130 words and no headings: name the offers being used and which have lasted longest, the angle the durable ads share, and the one thing worth testing first. Cite advertisers and day counts. If the long-running ads and the new ones point in different directions, say so - that gap is the finding. Do not describe the images; you cannot see them.
